t: Find the Losers of the Circular Game — Visited Simulation
o: Friend 1 starts with the ball; on turn i the holder passes i·k steps clockwise. Simulate until anyone receives the ball twice, then list friends never visited. Example 1: visits 1,3,2, then 3 again → losers [4,5]. Example 2: 1 passes 4 steps to itself → losers [2,3,4]. Positions map to friend ((pos−1) mod n)+1. n,k ≤ 50 makes direct simulation trivial.
k: Track visited friends; the pass distance grows by k each turn; stop on first repeat.
Clockwise stepping of d from friend f lands on ((f − 1 + d) mod n) + 1.

a.n: Approach 1: Straight simulation with a visited array
a.i: Maintain current friend and step multiplier; each pass computes the next friend via modular arithmetic, marking visits until a repeat occurs.
s: Mark friend 1 visited, current = 1, step = k.
Loop: next = ((current − 1 + step) mod n) + 1; if visited, stop; else mark and step += k.
a.t: O(n) — at most n successful receptions before a repeat terminates the game

w: Trivial simulation; the only care point is the modular friend-numbering formula. Follow-up: determine how many turns occur before the game ends, or generalize to counter-clockwise passing.
